transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-07
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Lena (EmberTech Head of ML), Rajiv (CTO), Ari (FinOps), Tanya (Infra), Mark (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): scoping conversation on pilot unit economics and benchmark plan. Customer has hard budget constraint and wants per-token estimates and concrete knobs (batch size, KV cache, quant) to hit cost targets.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone good to see you, thanks for making time. quick round of intros and objectives for today. we want to land on pilot scope and an initial cost model so your finance folks can sign off.
[00:18] Lena: thanks. main ask — we need to prove we can keep inference under our monthly ceiling, which is around 30k USD for the initial product surface, and hit p95 latency below 350 ms for single-turn completions of ~256 tokens. also want to see realistic throughput numbers.
[00:35] Rajiv: and security — we'll need KMS integration and audit logs, but AFAIK that's standard. pricing is the blocker.
[00:45] Maya: totally. we'll propose both hosted and dedicated variants. hosted gives fastest time-to-value; dedicated/quantized stacks are where you get the unit economics wins.
[01:10] Ari: just to be explicit — the budget Ari here — we can carve out a pilot pool but need a cap and clear expected USD per 1M tokens.
[01:25] Jordan: quick note on workloads — are you majority generation or embeddings? that changes tokens in vs tokens out and cost modeling.
[01:32] Mark: it's ~70% generation (assistant-style completions) and 30% semantic search embedding calls. generation average output length ~200 tokens, prompt avg ~120 tokens.
[01:45] Samir: ok so rough tokens per request ~320 tokens. at 10k req/day that's roughly 3.2M tokens/day, which scales fast.
[02:05] Lena: yeah that's why we need batching/kv caching explained — can you sketch how caching reduces token work?
[02:12] Maya: sure. KV cache (we sometimes see docs call it K-V cash, ha) saves prefix tokens when you have repeated context — in your chat use-case we estimate a 40-55% effective KV hit rate after a few turns. so that directly cuts generation tokens. also prefix caching for embeddings-heavy workflows can avoid re-encoding static context.
[02:40] Rajiv: do you have numbers on batching? our SLO requires median latency under 200ms for short completions, but we can tolerate higher tail latency if throughput improves.
[02:55] Maya: batching trades latency for throughput; with continuous batching in the runtime you can configure max batch latency window. in our tests a batch window of 20 ms with batch size target 8 gives ~2.5x efficiency versus no-batching for same GPU. if you increase to batch size 16 and allow 50 ms window, efficiency improves but p95 jumps. we can tune per-route.
[03:22] Tanya: infra question — for dedicated, what are network egress patterns and do we need private connectivity?
[03:30] Samir: we support VPC peering and private deployments; dedicated pools can sit in your account or Redwood-managed with private networking. for the pilot we usually run in Redwood-hosted dedicated with VPC peering.
[03:50] Lena: show us a worked example — per-1M tokens cost across host/dedicated/quantized.
[04:00] Samir: rough high-level numbers — hosted (baseline, no quant): $20-35 per 1M tokens depending on model size and context window. Dedicated, with batching and 4-bit quantization: effective cost can land in the $1.50-4 per 1M tokens range for steady-state workloads; the delta depends on your cache hit rate and batch size. these are order-of-magnitude numbers; we'll run a microbenchmark.
[04:32] Ari: that's a big range. can you break down where the savings come from?
[04:37] Maya: CPU/GPU amortization in dedicated pools, improved kernel paths for int4, less memory bandwidth per op, plus reduced tokens due to KV cache and repeated prefixes. also routing — sending low-latency small requests vs batching across async routes.
[04:55] Mark: curious — what's the baseline tokens/sec we should expect? our target is 2k-3k tokens/sec aggregate during busy windows.
[05:05] Jordan: depends on hardware and model family; for a 70B-ish model on an A100/RTX class you might see 300-800 tokens/sec single replica for generation in fp16; with quantization and batching you can push to 1k-2k tokens/sec per GPU. Redwood's autoscaler plus pooling gives aggregate higher numbers.
[05:35] Rajiv: and latency for 256-token output? p95 target 350 ms — realistic?
[05:40] Maya: for single-turn 256 tokens p95 350ms is tight for large models in hosted non-quantized mode; more realistic for optimized smaller models or quantized stacks. we can design a mixed strategy: route latency-sensitive traffic to smaller/opt models, bulk to higher-throughput variants.
[06:05] Lena: okay pilot success criteria — what would you want to measure?
[06:10] Samir: recommended success criteria list: 1) average cost per 1M tokens within agreed pilot ceiling, 2) p95 latency for canonical flows < 350ms, 3) caching reduces effective tokens by >=30%, 4) throughput meets 2k tokens/sec for peak windows, 5) no security gaps (KMS + audit logs validated).
[06:30] Ari: we need those in a spreadsheet with model assumptions — tokenization rates, batch sizes, cache hit assumptions.
[06:37] Samir: we'll deliver that.
[06:40] Mark: for benchmarks — what inputs do you need from us?
[06:43] Maya: sample prompts, representative traffic patterns (percentiles), and a small reproducible dataset so our harness can simulate. also whether you want cold-start vs warm cache scenarios.
[06:55] Tanya: we'll give an S3 bucket with test data and a temporary VPN, maybe a service account with read-only access.
[07:02] Samir: great. I'll drop a pilot plan: week 0 provisioning + security review; week 1 baseline hosted runs; week 2 dedicated/quant runs; week 3 tuning for batching and cache; week 4 consolidated report. then 6-week evaluation for business metrics.
[07:25] Rajiv: timeline looks fine, but approvals might push start out 2 weeks.
[07:30] Ari: we also need an explicit cap on the pilot spend so procurement can sign the order.
[07:35] Samir: we can proposal a capped pilot of $15k for the 4-week benchmark window — that'll cover hosted runs and a small dedicated burst. if you need lower we can shrink scope.
[07:46] Ari: I'll try to get that to $10k; please show a $10k and $15k scenario.
[07:52] Maya: noted.
[08:00] Mark: on metrics, please include token-level logging and per-route cost breakdowns. that's critical for FinOps.
[08:08] Samir: yup, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns and per-route model cost; we'll enable that for the pilot.
[08:15] Lena: any compliance red flags with the dedicated approach?
[08:19] Jordan: not for standard enterprise needs; we'll provide SOC2 docs, a network diagram, encryption-at-rest details, and KMS signing flow.
[08:30] Rajiv: what about model variants — will you fall back if a quant variant degrades quality?
[08:36] Maya: yes, we support model routing and automatic fallback to a higher-quality variant if quality metrics dip. we'll also instrument evals so you can see quality regressions on your prompt set.
[08:50] Ari: can you show an example cost calc? we want to see formula and assumptions.
[08:55] Samir: sure — example: assume 320 tokens/request, 100k requests/day => 32M tokens/day => 960M tokens/month. If hosted baseline is $25/1M => monthly cost ~ $24k. If dedicated with batching+quant reduces effective token work by 80% -> effective 192M tokens/month -> at $2/1M => $384. (note: big assumptions; exacts will vary).
[09:30] Mark: sounds promising but that 80% reduction is aggressive. what's the realistic expected reduction?
[09:36] Maya: realistic combined savings (batching + cache + quant) we usually see 40-60% on steady chat workflows; certain systems with repeated prefixes see more. we'll run conservative/optimistic scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[09:55] Lena: about quality — if quantized model changes completion quality we need to detect quickly. can we evaluate BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics?
[10:02] Maya: we'll run your prompt set through both variants and present side-by-side diffs and human-eval flags. we also support alerting on regeneration rates and unexpected token distribution changes.
[10:18] Rajiv: what are the observability artifacts we get? traces, per-token breakdown, per-route dashboards?
[10:24] Jordan: yes traces, per-route latency/cost, token breakdown, and raw logs (configurable). we can keep retention low for pilot.
[10:33] Tanya: network/perf — will you run benchmarks from our VPC or through Redwood endpoints?
[10:38] Samir: for fidelity we prefer running from your VPC (dedicated pilot) but we can also do an initial hosted run from Redwood region. Tanya, if you can open peering or provide a bastion and test creds that helps.
[10:56] Ari: procurement wants a one-pager on pilot deliverables and the approval path. can you include that with pricing?
[11:02] Samir: yes we'll include deliverables: benchmark harness, raw logs, cost model spreadsheet, quality eval, and runbook for rollout.
[11:12] Mark: any gotchas with token counting differences across tokenizers? we saw variance between model tokenizer and our pre-tokenizer.
[11:20] Maya: tokenizers differ — we'll standardize on the model tokenizer in benchmarks and include mapping of your current pre-tokenizer. differences can shift cost estimates; we'll highlight that in the sheet.
[11:33] Lena: ok, let's talk concrete numbers we'll run in the benchmark.
[11:36] Maya: propose these experiments: 1) baseline hosted run (no quant, minimal batching), 2) dedicated fp16 run with batching tuned, 3) dedicated int4 quant run, 4) cache-warm run measuring effective token reduction, 5) scale-up run to validate autoscaling and costs at 2k/3k tokens/sec. capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, tok-per-request, and USD per 1M token effective.
[12:05] Rajiv: how long does each experiment take?
[12:08] Maya: each can be done in 24 hours to get stable numbers, but we'll run multiple iterations; whole suite ~1 week if no infra delays.
[12:18] Ari: you mentioned model routing earlier — what are the Ops implications?
[12:22] Jordan: routing rules are policy configs; we can set per-route SLOs and fallback policies. Ops mainly needs to approve network and keys.
[12:30] Tanya: action on our side: get you VPN, S3, and a service account.
[12:34] Samir: actionable items we'll follow up in email.
[12:40] Mark: for the spreadsheet please include sensitivity checks: different KV hit rates (20/40/60%), batch sizes (1/8/16), and quantization levels (fp16/int8/int4).
[12:55] Maya: will do.
[13:00] Rajiv: final ask — show 10k and 15k pilot spend scenarios and what coverage each gives.
[13:06] Samir: yes. 10k covers baseline hosted runs and limited dedicated burst; 15k covers full 4-week suite and small dedicated capacity. we'll put explicit line items.
[13:20] Ari: timeline/next steps recap?
[13:23] Samir: Redwood sends pricing spreadsheet + benchmark harness (due 3/10-3/12). EmberTech shares dataset and VPN (due 3/11). Kickoff benchmark week starts after provisioning; target bench start 3/16 if approvals complete.
[13:40] Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[13:45] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and attach the plan.
